title: helm(private): validate values schema and improve init-hooks rollback compatibility
author: Mariana Lopez
description:
Background: the Private Helm chart init hooks have been the primary upgrade/rollback surface for in-place Private installs. Previous work introduced schema changes for private.values (git history: multiple init-hook refactors) but we saw regressions in rollbacks when CRDs/configmap ordering changed.

This PR does three things: 1) adds strict JSON Schema validation for the top-level private.values (with clear deprecation messages for removed keys), 2) updates the init hook ordering and tolerations so that rollback sequences don't deadlock on pending init jobs, and 3) adds a lightweight upgrade/rollback compatibility test harness to the chart tests so we catch regressions early.

Checklist:
- [x] Add schema for private.values and wire chart to validate on install/upgrade (helm template & unit tests)
- [x] Emit deprecation warnings for legacy keys (e.g. legacyNetwork.*)
- [x] Rework init hook Job -> Job+PodAntiAffinity and add backoff limit tweaks to allow deterministic rollback behavior
- [x] Add chart test which runs an upgrade -> rollback sequence using kind + local registry (CI mocked)
- [x] Update docs/values.md with examples and migration notes

Testing and validation: Local chart tests run with kind and the new compatibility harness (scripts/helm/test_compat.sh). CI runs the chart unit tests (lint, schema validation) and the full helm integration job on a linux runner with a mocked registry. Stress-tested a simulated failed upgrade path that previously left init hooks in Pending; after changes rollback completes cleanly in under 90s.

Backward compatibility: schema validation is opt-in via a new values key `schemaValidation.enabled` (defaults to true for new installs). When enabled on upgrades it will warn (non-fatal) for deprecated keys for one release cycle and fail on clearly invalid shapes. The init-hook ordering changes are compatible with existing clusters; the tolerations/backoff tweaks are conservative to avoid interfering with low-node-count installs.

Related: builds on prior PRs that refactored init-hooks and values schema (see pr-19730, pr-21027, pr-24199) and addresses incidents where rollbacks got blocked (internal incident SUP-1122).
